order_description: Respiratory assist device, bi-level pressure capability, without backup rate feature, used with noninvasive interface, e.g., nasal or facial mask (intermittent assist device with continuous positive airway pressure device)

candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: The order is for an E0470 (bi-level without backup rate) and the patient's documented diagnosis is obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 14, PSG 2026-08-30, no central events documented). L33718 specifically governs E0470 use for OSA and requires a failed E0601 trial before E0470 is covered. The record shows only a CPAP (E0601) order placed 2026-09-05 with no documented ineffective trial, so the E0470 request would not currently meet L33718 criterion D. L33800 is not the governing policy because it addresses hypoventilation, CSA, and COPD-related failure and defers OSA E0470 coverage to L33718.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: On 2026-08-18 Dr. Whitney250 Wiza601 saw the patient in person for evaluation of possible obstructive sleep apnea (R95). The attended in-laboratory polysomnography followed on 2026-08-30 (R38), so the evaluation came before the sleep test.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or, 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of: a. Excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or, b. Hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: The sleep study shows AHI 14 events/hour from 91 events over 6.5 hours of sleep, so alternative 1 (AHI of 15 or more) is not met. Alternative 2 applies (AHI 5 to 14 with at least 10 events), but the record does not document any qualifying condition. The patient denies daytime sleepiness, fatigue or trouble concentrating, has an Epworth score of 8 (R69), and has no insomnia, mood disorder, hypertension, ischemic heart disease or stroke history. Blood pressures were 127/77 and 123/80 (R57, R58). Stress and screening results do not establish a mood disorder.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: On 2026-09-11 a DME supplier documented instruction on the use and care of a CPAP device. The record names CPAP rather than the ordered E0470, so the device identity is not fully consistent, but the instruction on PAP use and care by the supplier is documented.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting.
criteria.explanation: The only PAP order is for an E0601 CPAP, placed 2026-09-05 and still active (R32, R96). The record documents no E0601 trial in a facility or at home and no documented failure to meet therapeutic goals. The E0470 order is therefore not supported by a failed E0601 trial. The 2026-09-05 note also says E0601 with a heated humidifier, which does not match the E0470 order.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The record documents an attended in-laboratory polysomnography (Type I, facility-based) on 2026-08-30 with a completed report, which is the sleep test type the policy accepts.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The polysomnography results (AHI 14 events/hour, 91 events over 6.5 hours) do not reach the AHI of 15 or more needed under alternative 1. Alternative 2 requires documented sleepiness, cognitive impairment, mood disorder, insomnia, hypertension, ischemic heart disease or stroke, and none is documented (see I.B).

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: The attended polysomnography was ordered by Dr. Whitney250 Wiza601 (R31), who is the treating practitioner documented in the 2026-08-18 visit where the sleep study was ordered (R95).

decision_explanation: Criterion I.B is not met because the sleep study AHI of 14 is below 15 and no qualifying symptom or comorbidity is documented for the 5 to 14 alternative. Criterion II.D is not met because no E0601 trial has been documented as tried and proven ineffective, and the only PAP order is for an E0601. Sleep Tests.3 is not met for the same reason as I.B. Criteria I.A, I.C, Sleep Tests.1 and Sleep Tests.4 are met. Sleep Tests.2 (FDA status) and Sleep Tests.5 (provider compliance) were excluded as administrative and regulatory. Continued coverage, replacement, oxygen and accessory sections do not apply at this initial order stage. Any one unmet criterion requires denial.
